Article Title: 'That's the world we live in': Travis Head breaks silence on wife's online abuse after Virat Kohli handshake row
Article Text:
Travis Head and Virat Kohli (ANI Photo)

Family affected by online abuse

NEW DELHI: Australia batter Travis Head has spoken publicly for the first time about the controversy involving Virat Kohli during the IPL 2026 match between Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB).The incident gained attention after cameras appeared to show RCB star Kohli skipping a handshake with SRH's Head after the game, leading to speculation about a rift between the two cricketers.Head, however, has dismissed the rumours, saying there was no issue to resolve."I don't think there's anything to patch over. That's just that's what it is. That's yeah. No surprises with how the competition went or what went on. So as expected," Head told Code Sports.The controversy took a personal turn when Head's wife, Jessica Davies, revealed she received abusive messages from fans on social media.Head admitted the online backlash was difficult, especially for his family, although he believes such attention is part of being a professional athlete."I think Jessica and I have a great perspective on things. That's the world we live in, and I think she's amazing in how she handles that kind of stuff.It was more the family stuff was built around it, flowing on to other family members who don't particularly see that sort of stuff," he said.Head also praised his wife for staying calm throughout the episode, adding, "Everyone forgets about it in a few days' time. She handled it extremely well. It's probably handling it with others and what other people's perspective of what things are like."Meanwhile, Kohli's Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defended their IPL title by defeating Gujarat Titans in the 2026 final in Ahmedabad.
Article Summary: Travis head speaks publicly for the first time about controversy involving virat kohli. Kohli skipped a handshake with srh's head after the game, leading to speculation about a rift. Head's wife, jessica davies, revealed she received abusive messages on social media.

Article Title: From selling vegetables to e-rickshaw driver, now India's first CWG 2026 medallist: How Bihar's Jhandu Kumar defied all odds
Article Text:
Jhandu Kumar (AP Photo)

From hardship to hope

The breakthrough that changed everything

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: For years, Jhandu Kumar's days began at a vegetable market and ended in a gym. When life became tougher during the COVID-19 pandemic, he swapped the market for an e-rickshaw, working long hours to support his family while refusing to give up on his dream of representing India.On Friday in Glasgow, that dream turned into reality.The 28-year-old para powerlifter from Bihar won bronze in the men's heavyweight event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, claiming India's first para powerlifting medal of the competition.As the medal was placed around his neck, the emotions of years of sacrifice came rushing back."I feel as if I'm flying. This is my first medal. Only one thing was going through my mind: that I have to win the medal. Just have to win," Jhandu told ANI.The journey to the Commonwealth podium was anything but easy.Affected by polio at the age of five, Jhandu battled both physical and financial challenges from an early age. His family's vegetable shop in Harnaut Bazaar, Nalanda district, was forced to shut temporarily during the pandemic due to the construction of an overbridge.To keep the household running, he began driving an e-rickshaw.Yet even then, training remained non-negotiable."Every day I used to travel nearly 20km to Bihar Sharif to buy vegetables, bring them back and sell them in the market. After finishing work around 4 pm, I would go to the gym for training," he had told TOI before the Games.Money was always tight. His daily earnings of Rs 400-500 barely covered household expenses, while protein supplements alone cost nearly Rs 1,000.Eventually, he sold his e-rickshaw in 2023 to compete at the National Para Powerlifting Championships, a gamble that initially failed after he could not register a successful lift.Instead of giving up, Jhandu caught the attention of national coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu, who invited him to train at the Sports Authority of India's National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar.That opportunity transformed his career. He went on to win silver at the inaugural Khelo India Para Games, followed by medals at national and international competitions, including bronze at the Asia-Oceania Open Para Powerlifting Championships.In Glasgow, Jhandu lifted 190kg to secure bronze after opening with 181kg. He even attempted a Commonwealth Games record of 196kg in his final lift, but fell just short.Despite missing the record, the medal meant everything."I'm very grateful that they let me practice so much and gave me so much love. I feel very good. I'll try to do even better in the future," he said.He also thanked the Sports Authority of India and the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) for backing his journey."I'm extremely grateful to them. We practice there, and this medal belongs to them, in a way," he said.For Jhandu Kumar, the bronze medal is more than a sporting achievement. It is proof that determination, sacrifice and unwavering belief can lift a person far beyond the weight on the bar.
Article Summary: Jhandu kumar won bronze in the men's heavyweight event at the 2026 commonwealth games. The 28-year-old para powerlifter from bihar battled both physical and financial challenges. His daily earnings of rs 400-500 barely covered household expenses, while protein supplements alone cost nearly rs 1,000.

Article Title: 'Why is he always retained?': Ashwin fires back at Mayank Yadav's critics
Article Text:
India's bowler Mayank Yadav (AP Photo/Wonder Mashura)

Mayank Yadav's return to international cricket could hardly have gone better, and former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes the young fast bowler deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries.Playing his first international match since October 2024, Mayank announced his comeback in style during the opening T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare. The speedster was named Player of the Match after producing a match-winning spell that began with a wicket off the very first ball of the contest.Mayank removed Brian Bennett for a duck with a hard-length delivery that straightened after pitching, forcing an outside edge that was safely taken behind the stumps. He continued to test Zimbabwe's batters with his pace and discipline, dismissing Dion Myers during the powerplay to leave the hosts under immediate pressure. His spell laid the platform for India's commanding bowling display.The performance marked a significant moment in the pacer's career after an injury-plagued period stalled his rapid rise. Initially fast-tracked into the Indian side as part of the team's long-term plans for the 2026 T20 World Cup, Mayank spent the past two years battling recurring fitness issues that repeatedly interrupted his progress.Speaking on 'Ash ki Baat', Ashwin reflected on the challenges of returning from multiple injuries and urged fans to avoid judging players too quickly."It is not easy to go through a stress fracture at a young age. We often see and think, why is he always retained? He is always injured. We easily tell this. No player plays to get injured. Injury can be very painful. It is not just physical but also a mental barrier, especially if you are injured twice. It is not easy on the body. If it resurfaces, it plays on your mind. Mayank Yadav has a lot of time and is exceptionally talented. I want him to play more," he said on 'Ash ki Baat'.Ashwin also acknowledged India's convincing start to the series and congratulated new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer on securing his maiden victory as skipper."Congratulations to Shreyas for the first win. He would have been searching for it. There is not a lot to see when you restrict Zimbabwe to 120-odd. Mayank, Prince, and Ashok all got an opportunity," he said.Mayank's impressive return has not only revived India's pace options but also reinforced why he continues to be viewed as one of the country's most exciting fast-bowling prospects when fully fit.
Article Summary: Ravichandran ashwin believes mayank yadav deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries. Mayank announced his comeback in style during the opening t20i against zimbabwe. The speedster was named player of the match after producing a match-winning spell that began with a wicket off the very first ball of the contest.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work” - How LeBron James walked away from $50M to chase on
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work” - How LeBron James walked away from $50M to chase one final NBA dream (Image via Getty)

Why LeBron James gave up millions to keep chasing another NBA title

Why LeBron James nearly retired before finding one more reason to play

Why LeBron James joins Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia

Dreams and Nightmares

LeBron James is proving passion can matter more than money

At 41, LeBron James has already achieved everything most basketball players only dream about. He is the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, a four-time champion and a four-time Finals MVP. He could have stayed in Los Angeles on a salary worth more than $50 million a season or simply called time on one of the greatest careers in sports. Instead, he made a choice that surprised even longtime fans. LeBron left the money behind and joined the Philadelphia 76ers because he still believes he has one more championship run left in him. As he prepares for a record-breaking 24th NBA season, he has made it clear that winning, not money, is what drives him now.LeBron’s move to Philadelphia was about much more than changing teams. It was about choosing competition over comfort.During his final season with the Los Angeles Lakers, he earned more than $50 million. With the 76ers, he signed a two-year veteran-minimum contract that pays $3.88 million for the 2026-27 season and includes a $4.07 million player option for 2027-28. The deal is worth just under $8 million in total, and his salary takes up only a small part of Philadelphia’s salary cap.That decision gives the 76ers more financial flexibility to build a team capable of winning another championship.Soon after announcing his decision, LeBron explained exactly why money was never part of the conversation. “This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.”A few months earlier, LeBron was not thinking about another team. He was thinking about retirement.After the Lakers were knocked out of the playoffs, he stepped away from the spotlight and gave himself time to decide whether he still wanted to continue playing. Around the same time, the Lakers were moving into a new era after their blockbuster trade for Luka Dončić in 2025, changing the franchise’s long-term direction.Looking back on that period, LeBron admitted he had almost reached the end of his journey.“I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn’t ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game… I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game. I still truly love this game, and I have more to give.”Those weeks away from basketball helped him realise that his love for the game had not disappeared. Instead of retiring, he found one more goal worth chasing.LeBron’s smaller contract also helped Philadelphia strengthen its roster.The 76ers already had Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey before making one of the biggest moves of the offseason by acquiring reigning Finals MVP Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics in exchange for Paul George and future draft picks.When LeBron announced his move on Instagram, he shared a career highlight video set to Meek Mill’s. The final moment of the video ended with a line that perfectly matched the start of this new chapter.“Hold up, wait a minute, y’all thought I was finished?”If Philadelphia wins the NBA championship, LeBron would become the first player in NBA history to win NBA titles with four different franchises after previously lifting the trophy with the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers and Los Angeles Lakers.Very few athletes get to decide how their story ends. Even fewer choose the harder path when an easier one is available.LeBron could have finished his career without taking another big challenge. Instead, he chose a new city, a new locker room and fresh expectations because he still wants to compete for the biggest prize in basketball.His decision is not just about one more season. It is about staying true to the reason he started playing in the first place. More than two decades after entering the NBA, LeBron is still willing to sacrifice, work and grind for the chance to feel what winning another championship is like. That mindset, more than any record or contract, is what continues to define his remarkable career.
Article Summary: Lebron james joined the philadelphia 76ers on a two-year veteran-minimum contract that pays $3.88 million for the 2026-27 season and includes a $4.07 million player option for 2027-28. The deal is worth just under $8 million in total, and his salary takes up only a small part of philadelphia’s salary cap.

Article Title: The story behind the Champion: “I never saw my mother happy with me and proud of me for doing something, I never got a chance to talk to her or know about her” - Mike Tyson on the complicated relation

Mike Tyson has opened up about the controversial life his mother lived before she tragically passed away before he became famous

Mike Tyson, one of the boxing legends in the world, came from a poverty stricken household before he made it in the world of boxing. While poverty was a constant issue he faced in his childhood, Mike Tyson’s relationship with his mother remained a pretty complicated one before she passed away tragically even before he became famous.In an interview with Bleacher Report, Mike Tyson reflected on the bond he had with his mother as he said, “I never saw my mother happy with me and proud of me for doing something…”The boxing legend added, “She only knew me as being a wild kid running the streets, coming home with new clothes that she knew I didn’t pay for.”The popular entrepreneur continued, “I never got a chance to talk to her or know about her. Professionally, it has no effect, but it’s crushing emotionally and personally.”This was not the first time that Mike Tyson opened up about his mother in interviews.In another interview with Shannon Sharpe on his Shay Shay Podcast, Mike Tyson opened up about his mother’s death as he said, "You know, one of the best things that ever happened to me is that my mother died.”The boxing legend added, “Because my mother would have made me babies. There's no way I would ever get into a street fight. Article Title: Underprepared East Bengal and Mohun Bagan kick-off new season with Durand Cup opener
Article Text:
Mohun Bagan vs East Bengal (PTI Photo)

KOLKATA: India’s oldest football tournament is hours away from an odd and unprecedented beginning. However, kick-starting the Durand Cup with a Kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th-year-old history has its own hype and hazards. Because, the blockbuster match between East Bengal FC and Mohun Bagan SG at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday will also set in motion the start of India’s domestic football season as well and the hard truth is that both teams look oddly underprepared.Let’s fix our gaze on some strange layers of the match. ISL champions East Bengal and runners-up Mohun Bagan — now under new coaches Antonio Lopez Habas and Panagiotis Dilmperis respectively — have hit the training ground running only four days ago. Not to mention the fact that while Habas will have only newcomer Dani Ramirez and old hand Mohammad Rashid available for selection, Dilmperis’ cupboard looks emptier with Serbian forward Dejan Drazic being the only foreigner to take part in Friday’s pre-match training session — a strange departure from the past when overseas players have predominantly emerged as show-stealers in such duels. It’s somewhat fitting that domestic players will now get the kind of spotlight they are rarely granted, thereby giving this season-opening derby primarily an indigenous spine."We haven't had enough time to train. It's impossible to prepare properly for such an important match in just a few days,” Habas admitted on Friday. "Our idea is to make the team solid, compact and competitive. We need time to develop our model of play, but that's the foundation we want to build," he added.It’s a strange but emotionally-charged homecoming for the 69-year-old Spaniard, who holds a rare link to the inaugural season of ISL and has guided now defunct ATK to two titles and Mohun Bagan to an ISL winner’s Shield.“I have absolute respect for Mohun Bagan and for everything we achieved together. I have wonderful memories of the fans and my time in Kolkata. But now I have another job, another responsibility. I have to fight for my new team," Habas said.His counterpart, Dilmperis — fondly called Panos — is also bracing for a challenging debut. Having made his mark as Punjab FC coach, the 51-year-old Greek couldn’t have asked for a toucher test for his coronation as Bagan coach.“Starting my journey with a derby is exciting because this is why football exists. Football is about rivalries, competition, and passion. Joining a club like Mohun Bagan, with its incredible fan base, rich history, ambitious ownership, and high expectations, is not pressure for me—it is a huge source of motivation," Panos remarked.“For me, every match is a derby. Whether we are playing the team at the top of the table or the bottom, I prepare with the same intensity,” he maintained.The last time a domestic tournament began with a derby happened way back in the 2004-2005 season of I-League. However, by that time, both teams had already gone through the grind of the local league.Starved of adequate time to pass muster, both teams are facing a whole new ball game. The likes of Bipin Singh, Edmund Lalrindika and David Lalhlansanga in the upfront as well as Jeakson Singh and Anwar Ali in defence contributed immensely to East Bengal’s march to the ISL summit last season. They will again be tasked with a new challenge of rising to the occasion.For Bagan, Liston Colaco, Manvir Singh and Sahal Abdul Samad will again be central to the team’s ambitions.However, it may threaten to float away into its own strange space; this season-opening derby with essentially a rare desi look will have the odds stacked against no team. It’s floating along the usual 50-50 narrative.
Article Summary: The durand cup kicks off with a kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th-year-old history. Isl champions east bengal and runners-up mohun bagan have hit the training ground running only four days ago. Both teams look oddly underprepared.

Article Title: India eye series win vs Zimbabwe: Can Abhishek Sharma break his lean run?
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma (ANI Photo)

After the bruising their T20 side endured on the UK tour, this Zimbabwe series could be just the ideal fillip India needed.Having finally recorded their maiden win under new T20 captain Shreyas Iyer after seven winless matches at the helm, India will look to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead when they take on Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Saturday.Following a difficult run that saw them whitewashed by Ireland (0-2) and England (0-4), India’s convincing sevenwicket victory in the seriesopener has restored some much-needed confidence.Yet, even as the visitors look to build on that momentum, one player who will be under the scanner is explosive opener Abhishek Sharma.Two years ago, Harare was the venue where Abhishek announced himself on the international stage with a breathtaking maiden T20I hundred in only his second game.The stylish left-hander returns to the same ground searching for a spark after a worrying dip in form. Having begun the England series promisingly with scores of 59 and 43, Abhishek’s returns thereafter have read 10, 16, 3 and 1. In Thursday’s opener, his uncomfortable eight-ball 1 suggested a batter short on rhythm and confidence.With competition for places intensifying, Abhishek knows he needs runs. Senior opener Sanju Samson, though absent on this tour, remains in the selectors’ plans and has been named in India’s squad for the Asian Games later this year.A substantial score in Harare would not only help India seal the series but also strengthen Abhishek’s own case in a rapidly evolving T20 setup.India, though, found a new hero in the opening match.Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed a stunning 18-ball fifty, becoming the youngest player to score a T20I half-century.The 15-year-old, who had endured a difficult England tour where pacy bowlers like Jofra Archer tested him relentlessly with short-pitched bowling, responded in style against Zimbabwe.Taking on Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani fearlessly, he produced a blistering innings that underlined why he is so highly rated.Supported by Ishan Kishan’s brisk 35 and an unbeaten 28 from skipper Iyer, Sooryavanshi ensured India chased down the target with more than six overs to spare.Head coach VVS Laxman would have been equally pleased by the performance of India’s revamped pace attack. The biggest positive was the return of Mayank Yadav, who made an impressive comeback after two injury-ravaged years. The Delhi quick finished with figures of 2 for 18 and consistently touched high speeds, with his opening delivery to Brian Bennett at 150 kmph indidcating that his pace remains intact.Prince Yadav also showed signs of improvement after a lean England tour, while debutant Ashok Sharma displayed enough promise to suggest he could become another exciting fast-bowling option.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Nico Williams: "I run very fast, but I can't run as fast as my mother. Because she once escaped death and…" - an emotional tribute to his mother, the extraordinary journey behind h
Article Text:
Nico Williams (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Nico Williams

"I run very fast, but I can't run as fast as my mother. Because she once escaped death and crossed the Sahara Desert from Ghana to Spain to become who I am today. I gave the medal to my mother because she deserves it more than anyone else"

The moment behind the quote by Nico William

What the comparison is actually saying

Why he gave the medal away

Why sacrifice so often stays invisible behind success

Why this quote still resonates beyond football

A winner's medal usually gets read as proof of what an athlete just achieved on the pitch. Nico Williams, the Spanish footballer, read his differently. "I run very fast, but I can't run as fast as my mother," he said. "Because she once escaped death and crossed the Sahara Desert from Ghana to Spain to become who I am today. I gave the medal to my mother because she deserves it more than anyone else." A medal earned in ninety minutes was, in his own telling, connected to a much longer and harder journey that began decades earlier, long before he was born, on a route that plenty of people crossing it did not survive. His gesture transformed a personal sporting achievement into a powerful tribute to sacrifice, resilience and the countless struggles his family overcame before reaching a safer future. The story is a poignant reminder that behind many public successes lie unseen sacrifices, with achievements often built upon the courage and determination of those who came before us.Williams said this after Spain's Euro 2024 victory over England in July 2024, a tournament in which he scored the opening goal of the final and was named one of the standout performers of the whole competition. He was born in Pamplona, Spain, to Ghanaian parents, and his older brother, Iñaki Williams, plays international football for Ghana rather than Spain.The family's migration story, crossing the Sahara before eventually settling in Spain, sits directly behind both brothers' careers.Williams is known specifically for his speed on the pitch, which makes the comparison land harder than it otherwise might. He is not measuring his mother's journey against his own athletic pace literally. He is arguing that the courage and endurance it took her to survive that crossing outweighs anything he has done as a professional footballer, however fast he happens to be able to run.Plenty of athletes dedicate a win to their families in general terms. Williams did something more specific, treating the medal as something connected directly to his mother's own sacrifice rather than solely to his own performance. In his framing, the achievement had more than one author, his training and effort on one side, and the earlier decisions and hardship that made his life in Spain possible on the other.A medal is visible. A goal gets replayed endlessly. The decisions and hardship that came years earlier, the ones that actually made the achievement possible in the first place, rarely get the same attention. Williams' quote pulls that hidden part of the story directly into view, refusing to let his own success stand apart from what his parents went through to give him the chance at it. It serves as a reminder that behind many celebrated sporting moments lies a family's quiet sacrifice, years of persistence, financial struggles and unwavering belief that often remain unseen long after the applause fades.Plenty of people carry family histories shaped by migration and hardship they did not personally experience but still benefit from directly. Williams' quote gives that quiet inheritance a specific, public voice, treating his own visible success as something built on a far less visible journey that came before it.
Article Summary: Spanish footballer nico williams gave away his euro 2024 medal to his mother. He was born in pamplona, spain, to ghanaian parents. His older brother, iñaki williams, plays international football for ghana. The family's migration story, crossing the sahara, sits directly behind both brothers' careers.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Lamine Yamal: "My mother had me at 16, and my father searched for ways to..." - a powerful lesson on perspective, family sacrifice and why football is not the hardest battle his fa
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal

Quote of the day by Lamine Yamal

"My mother had me at 16, and my father searched for ways to bring food home. That's real pressure. All I have to do is play football"

The moment behind Lamine Yamal’s quote

The family story behind the words

What the comparison is actually doing

Why this reflects more than modesty

Other things Lamine Yamal has said

"It moves me to see my brother so happy, to see my mother living the life she's always dreamed of, and my friends, too. It's a child's greatest dream."

"I'm in love with my little brother. I love him like a son."

Why this still resonates beyond football

Pressure gets discussed constantly in football, usually about missed chances and expectant crowds. Lamine Yamal, Spain's teenage forward, measured his own pressure against something else entirely. "My mother had me when she was 16, that's real pressure," he said. "My father had to figure out life, going out to the street to pick things up. All I have to do is play football." Asked to explain the weight of carrying a national team, he pointed the question straight back at his own family, refusing to let his own circumstances, remarkable as they already were at nineteen, be treated as the hardest thing anyone in his family had actually lived through, given everything his parents had gone through years before he ever kicked a ball professionally. His perspective is a reminder that gratitude and perspective can reshape how we view our own challenges, making even the biggest stages seem smaller when compared with the sacrifices that made them possible.Yamal said this in the build-up to Spain's run at the 2026 World Cup, a tournament Spain went on to win, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final at MetLife Stadium on 19 July, only days after Yamal turned nineteen. Pushed on the pressure of leading the team, he redirected the question entirely: "Don't paint me as if what I'm experiencing is the real pressure.There are people who have endured far more." His response reflected a maturity beyond his age, showing that he viewed football success through the lens of perspective, gratitude and respect for those facing greater struggles.Accordinf to reports, his mother, Sheila Ebana, moved to Catalonia from Bata, Equatorial Guinea, and had Yamal at sixteen. His father, Mounir Nasraoui, arrived in Spain from Morocco as a young child and later worked scrap collection and other temporary jobs to get by. The couple separated when Yamal was around three, and he grew up largely in Rocafonda, a working-class neighbourhood in Mataró, in a small flat where the kitchen and bedroom were effectively one room.Yamal is not describing professional football as easy. Reaching the top of the sport by nineteen required years of relentless training and competing against far older, more experienced players. What he is doing is placing that effort next to a different kind of pressure entirely, the pressure of becoming a parent at sixteen, or of scraping together enough money to keep a family fed. Next to that, he treats his own job, difficult as it genuinely is, as something closer to a privilege than a burden.Public success can easily narrow someone's view until their own difficulties feel like the only ones that matter. Yamal's comment does the opposite. Despite being one of the most closely watched young players in the world, he places his own challenge inside the context of what his parents actually went through to give him the chance at it in the first place.Most people compare their own struggles to someone else's at some point, and it rarely makes the struggle disappear. What it can do is add context. Yamal's own difficulty, performing under enormous public attention at nineteen, is genuinely real. He has simply chosen to measure it against something he considers larger, and decided his own job looks smaller by comparison.
Article Summary: Lamine yamal, spain's teenage forward, measured his own pressure against something else entirely. Asked to explain the weight of carrying a national team, he pointed the question straight back at his own family. His response reflected a maturity beyond his age, showing that he viewed football success through the lens of perspective.

Article Title: Quote of the day by David Beckham: "I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to…" - a powerful lesson on hard work, discipline and why talent alone is never
Article Text:
David Beckham

Quote of the day by David Beckham

"I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more"

What is the meaning behind David Beckham’s quote

Why talent alone rarely gets someone all the way there

Why setbacks tested this philosophy directly

Why consistency matters more than occasional motivation

Other famous quotes by David Beckham

"The secret to my success is practice!"

"The secret of the team's success is easy, unity and hard work."

"You will go through tough times, it's about getting through them."

"I don't have time for hobbies. At the end of the day, I treat my job as a hobby. It's something I love doing."

Why it still feels relevant today

People tend to admire success from a safe distance, seeing the trophy without ever seeing the years that produced it. David Beckham summed up his own version of that gap plainly. "I have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more," he said. The repetition is not accidental. He is describing something continuous, not a single burst of effort that happens once and then stops. Coming from a player often remembered for his technique on free kicks and crosses, the line carries the weight of someone who actually built that skill through repetition, rather than someone simply repeating a motivational slogan he never had to test himself. His journey from a young academy player to a global football icon reflects the discipline, patience and relentless commitment required to turn natural ability into lasting excellence on the biggest stages. The quote serves as a timeless reminder that extraordinary achievements are rarely the result of talent alone, but of consistent effort sustained long after the initial excitement has faded.The phrase "anything special in life" is deliberately broad, applying just as easily to a career in business or medicine as it does to professional sport. The answer he gives is repeated three times for a reason, work, work, work some more, because Beckham is not describing hard work as an occasional event.He is describing it as the actual, unglamorous rhythm behind lasting achievement.Natural ability offers a real head start, but plenty of gifted people never fully develop it, while plenty of less naturally talented people outwork their way past them over time. Former teammates and coaches have repeatedly described Beckham staying behind after regular training to practise free kicks and crosses long after everyone else had gone home, which is really the practical version of the quote in action.Beckham faced serious public criticism at points in his career, most famously after being sent off during England's 1998 World Cup exit to Argentina. He later described that period bluntly. "I have nightmares about France 98," he said. "It was humiliating. It will always be with me." Rather than letting that moment define the rest of his career, he kept working and went on to become one of England's most recognised footballers, a direct example of the same principle behind today's quote.Motivation naturally rises and falls, strong some days and completely absent on others. Discipline is what keeps someone working through the days motivation does not show up, which is really the difference between an ambition that stays an idea and one that eventually becomes a career.Modern culture often makes success look instant, a single viral moment or a sudden breakthrough. Beckham's own career is a reminder that most of what actually produces lasting results happens quietly, well before anyone else is paying attention, repeated on ordinary days long after the initial excitement of starting has worn off.
Article Summary: "i have always believed that if you want to achieve anything special in life you have to work, work, and then work some more" - david beckham. The quote serves as a timeless reminder that extraordinary achievements are rarely the result of talent alone. Discipline is what keeps someone working through the days motivation does not show up.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.
